notes: All 5,323 source rows in both pinned OUP-branded PDFs were parsed and independently validated; none were skipped as vocabulary. Oxford 5000 PDF explicitly supplies the extension to Oxford 3000, rather than a separate combined list.

The named Oxford 5000 list does not imply exactly 5,000 distinct spellings. Homographs, senses, word classes and level-specific rows change the count. This artifact does not inflate the count using inflected forms, invented words, or duplicate cards.

Oxford 3000 PDF yields exactly 3,000 distinct source homograph labels; extension PDF yields 1,999. Seventeen source homograph labels and twenty spelling groups overlap between PDFs. Across both PDFs: 4,982 distinct source homograph labels and 4,955 distinct spelling groups.

Different spellings sharing a casefold key are intentionally preserved: May/may, March/march and IT/it. A comma-separated a, an remains one source headword; phrase entries such as according to, have to, ice cream and used to remain intact.

TXT files in the same mirror are unsuitable as authority for an exact PDF-completeness count: they lowercase many names, truncate according to to according, omit multiword entries, add accounting/angrily/cleaning/feeding and differ on disk/inquiry and proceedings. The PDF rows are the retained source of headword/POS/CEFR facts.
Source rows include factual headword, POS and CEFR data only. No Oxford definitions, examples, audio or IPA were fetched or copied.

Publisher-hosted PDF endpoints were not verified: the existing acquisition audit reports HTTP403. This is complete against the pinned mirror PDFs, not a guarantee of identity with the current publisher edition.

fullVocabularyReview.scope: Explicit selected meanings and original bilingual contexts reviewed against directly read source evidence. Historical word-list facts are preserved separately; this is not publisher certification or a claim to cover every sense.

essentialSenses.scope: Ordered additive essential-sense reviews; each batch retains its own baseline, source evidence and editorial scope.
